_what: Caution markers per 1000 words, per submission text, at the moment this was pinned. A readability pass may raise it; a FALL is what --check refuses.
_why: A revision that reads better because a hedge, a null or a limitation quietly left is worse than the dense original — it is now readable AND overstated, and on a posted paper it is overstated under a DOI.
_regenerate: python3 research/manuscripts/lint_readability.py --write-baseline, and say in the commit message which qualification changed and why.

_why_each_entry_exists.research/manuscripts/care-delivery/emc-t: ⛔ PINNED 2026-09-02 BECAUSE ITS ABSENCE MADE CLAUSE 7 PASS ON A CHECK IT NEVER RAN. `publish_bar.clause_7` reads `was = baseline.get(doc)` and then guards the caution-drop test with `if was is not None`, so a paper with no entry skipped that half entirely and returned PASS. The clause was honest about it — its evidence line printed '(no baseline pinned)' — but the half that catches a readability pass BUYING clarity with a hedge, a null or a limitation simply did not run. ★ THIS PAPER WAS ONE CLAUSE FROM POSTABLE WHEN THAT WAS NOTICED, which is why it is pinned before the last clause is closed rather than after: 7/7 on a bar with a vacuous clause is the 'status that looks like a measurement' defect at the one door that opens outward. ⚠ 12.8 IS THE MEASURED VALUE AT THIS COMMIT, not a target and not a floor anyone chose. It can only cause a future FAIL, never a future PASS, so pinning it is a strengthening — and it is pinned at the value the paper actually has so that the first thing it catches is a real regression rather than an arbitrary bar. Raising it later to clear a run would be exactly what `amendment_guard` refuses.
